items.stem: You need the total of Sales where Region is 'North' and Quarter is 'Q1'. Which function fits best?

options.rationale: Correct: SUMIFS sums with multiple conditions, one criterion per range.
SUMIF takes only a single criterion.
That does not aggregate conditionally across rows the way SUMIFS does.
COUNTIFS counts rows; it does not total a value.

items.stem: A VLOOKUP returns #N/A for unmatched codes and you want a clean report. Which TWO are sound ways to handle it? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: IFERROR substitutes a friendly value when the lookup fails.

options.text: Investigate whether the missing codes indicate a real data problem
options.rationale: Correct: suppressing the symbol is not enough; genuine gaps should be understood.

options.text: Delete every row that shows #N/A without checking
options.rationale: Deleting data blindly can remove legitimate records.
That stops all results updating, not just the error.

items.stem: LEFT(A2,3) returns the first three characters of a phone number, but a later SUM of that column fails. Why?

options.text: LEFT returns text, so the extracted values are not numbers
options.rationale: Correct: text-returning functions produce text; convert with VALUE or multiply by 1 if numbers are needed.
LEFT works on text and text representations of numbers.
SUM can read any column; the issue is the data type.
Merging is unrelated to the text-vs-number cause here.
